Hope you had a good week. We're finalizing an internal one-pager for product and sales that summarizes how Redwood handles subprocessors and cross-border transfers for the hosted API. Legal at Acme has asked for a short, customer-facing blurb (2-3 sentences) we can include in our procurement materials and link to from our security questionnaire.

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear ask. See a first pass below and attached (proposed_blurb_v1.txt). Happy to iterate with legal and content for tone.

One-line (console tooltip / sales):
"Redwood uses a limited set of subprocessors to operate the hosted API and applies contractual safeguards and standard data-transfer protections for cross-border processing."

2–3 sentence paragraph (FAQ / procurement):
"Redwood operates a small, vetted set of subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, telemetry vendors) that help deliver the hosted API. We contractually require subprocessors to follow our security and confidentiality requirements, and we employ industry-standard protections for cross-border transfers (encryption in transit and at rest, and contractual safeguards such as SCCs where applicable). Customers can request our current subprocessor list and detailed transfer mechanisms via the Console or through their account manager."

Thanks Ben — nice draft. A few edits from Legal for accuracy and to reduce implied commitments: please see inline edits and an alternative suggested wording below. Also attaching the current subprocessor list we can share with vetted customers (redwood_subprocessor_list_2028-01.pdf).

Edits / rationale (high-level):
- Avoid claiming we "employ SCCs" as a blanket statement; say "we rely on appropriate transfer mechanisms (e.g., SCCs) where required".
- Call out SOC 2 and optional KMS to signal controls without promising specific configurations to every customer.
- Make the console tooltip very short to fit UI constraints.

Suggested final wording: 
Tooltip (short):
"Redwood uses a vetted set of subprocessors and contractual safeguards for customer data."

FAQ paragraph (2–3 sentences):
"Redwood works with a limited, vetted set of subprocessors (for example, cloud infrastructure and monitoring providers) to operate the hosted API. We require subprocessors to meet Redwood's security and confidentiality standards and we maintain SOC 2 controls. For cross-border processing we rely on appropriate transfer mechanisms where required (e.g., SCCs) and protect data in transit and at rest; customers requiring customer-managed keys can opt into KMS integrations. The current subprocessor list and more detail on transfer safeguards are available on request via the Console or your account team."

Laura / Naomi — can you review the tone for sales and UI constraints? If this looks good to Acme, we can attach the PDF and provide the HubSpot link Kimberly referenced.
